audit.why: TRICKY / 7.5-10 with a 9.5/10 carry rating fits a lane Nautilus dominates for ten minutes and then cannot touch. The 63.64% figure rests on 11 Emerald+ games and is far too thin to raise the rating.

audit.whatIsWrong: Rows 0, 1, 2 and 4 gave the lane to Kayle or to Skill while the whys on the same rows describe Nautilus winning outright, and both the packet chart and the already-completed mirror audit read Nautilus/Nautilus/Skill/Skill/Kayle/Kayle/Kayle.
audit.why: whys[0] 'your passive root on the first auto wins the level 1 trade outright' and whys[1] 'Your Q anchor pulls her in with no escape' cannot sit under a Kayle or Skill row. whys[2] describes a stalemate (you shred, she tucks under tower) = Skill. whys[4] 'Her R invulnerability eats your Depth Charge knock-up' = Kayle.
audit.corrected: Rows 0 and 1 flipped to Nautilus (ratings 8/10), row 2 to Skill (6/10), row 4 to Kayle, proposed as matched full+content pairs, with the four why strings rewritten to state the real reason.

audit.whatIsWrong: The packet flags that the page names almost none of Kayle's kit, and two decisive interactions were absent: Celestial Blessing (W) heals her on a flat 15s cooldown, and Starfire Spellblade (E) is an auto-attack reset that tells you the burst is starting.
audit.why: enemyKit W: 'Kayle heals and grants Move Speed to herself and the nearest ally', cd 15 flat — the missingInteractions file flags needs-antiheal for exactly this pairing, and the page only says 'his healing fights your grind' without naming the spell. enemyKit E carries the autoReset flag: the wind-up, not the cast, is the cue. Divine Judgment's 160s rank-1 cooldown is the number that makes 'bait it' actionable.
audit.corrected: Celestial Blessing named with its 15s cooldown and tied to Grievous Wounds in dontsFull[0].d; Starfire Spellblade's auto reset and Divine Judgment's 160s cooldown written into report[5].t; Dredge Line's 14s rank-1 cooldown put into phases[1].why.

edits.before: Passive-root auto trades win the first exchanges. Identify how Kayle contests the first waves before you commit anything.
edits.after: Passive-root auto trades win the first exchanges. Kayle is a melee with no dash and no Celestial Blessing yet — walk at her.

edits.before: Hook threat changes where he can stand forever. Only take the trade when Kayle's Divine Judgment is down.
edits.after: Dredge Line is up every 14s at rank 1 — land it and a dashless Kayle cannot walk out of your E slow.

edits.before: Full kit online — your core pattern starts now. Keep the wave near your side so Kayle must walk into your engage range.
edits.after: Full kit online — W burn and E slow shred her. She answers by tucking under tower to farm, so deny the last-hits.

edits.before: Depth Charge is an unmissable point-click knockup — the all-in always starts. Reassess every all-in at 6 — Kayle's ultimate changes the math too.
edits.after: Depth Charge cannot miss, but Divine Judgment makes her invulnerable through the knockup — bait the 160s ult or your all-in resolves into nothing.

edits.before: Track Kayle's Divine Judgment (Invuln): Her get-out at 6. Bait it. When it is down — Q-E + R her.
edits.after: Divine Judgment is 160s at rank 1 — bait it, then Q-E-R. Starfire Spellblade's auto reset is her burst tell.

edits.before: That is Kayle's favourite window — refuse it and half his win condition is gone.
edits.after: Celestial Blessing heals her every 15s — deny the CS and buy Grievous before the grind.

notes: The full layer calls Kayle 'he/his' in tradeGood, dontsFull[0], breakdown.feeding, report[8] and report[12] — template artefact, not a fact error, left alone. Divine Judgment makes the ALLY invulnerable (she can cast it on herself or a team-mate) and rains swords in an area; the page treats it purely as her self-peel, which is right for a 1v1 but understates it in teamfights. Dredge Line's derived 'terrain' flag reads 'creates terrain, blocks paths and dashes' — that contradicts Riot's description, where colliding with terrain pulls Nautilus toward it. Followed the description, as the mirror did.
